content: Stainless steel contains at least 5% chromium by mass. This material is less prone to staining, corrosion, and rust compared to ordinary steel, which is why it is referred to as stainless. However, it is not completely resistant to staining. In contexts where the specific alloy type and grade are not specified, particularly in the aviation industry, it is also called corrosion-resistant steel. Stainless steel is available in various grades and surface finishes, which are tailored to the environmental conditions the material will encounter during its use. Common applications of stainless steel include cutlery and watch straps. The primary distinction between stainless steel and carbon steel lies in the chromium content. Carbon steel tends to rust when exposed to air and moisture, as it forms an active iron oxide layer. This layer accelerates further corrosion by promoting the formation of additional iron oxide. In contrast, stainless steel contains enough chromium to form a passive layer of chromium oxide on its surface. This passive film acts as a protective barrier, preventing further corrosion.
